defect.evidence_quote: It is therefore now up to the Court of Appeals to decide whether, at each step of the search process, the warrant satisfied the Fourth Amendment’s requirements of particularity and probable cause.
defect.problem: The search-threshold holding is supported, but the remand clause is too broad as phrased: the Court left the reasonableness of this multi-step warrant/search process for remand, not whether geofence warrants as a class satisfy probable cause and particularity.
defect.proposed_fix: Change the final clause to: "the Court did not decide whether the multi-step geofence warrant at issue satisfied probable cause and particularity, vacating and remanding."

reasons: The opinion states that police conducted a search when they gained access to Location History data.
The opinion states that an individual has a reasonable expectation of privacy in records about his cell phone’s location, even for a limited time and from a third-party tech company.
The disposition was vacated and remanded, but the remanded warrant question was case-specific and step-specific.
residual_risks: No separate inventory row asked for quote-fidelity review of the Rule quote or pin-op.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Specify "the warrant at issue" and "at each step of the search process" for the probable-cause/particularity remand.

reasons: The opinion is centrally about a geofence warrant directed to Google Location History.
The opinion explains the geofence process and resolves the search-threshold question for Location History data.
residual_risks: The role label is editorial taxonomy, but it is supported by the disclosed opinion.

reasons: The holding expressly turns on a reasonable expectation of privacy in cell-phone location information.
The opinion states police invade that expectation when they acquire Location History, even for a limited time and via a third-party tech company.
The opinion repeatedly applies Carpenter’s CSLI reasoning to Google Location History.

The opinion expressly rejects applying the third-party doctrine to Location History, reasoning that Carpenter refused to apply it to CSLI and no good reason exists to treat Location History differently.
residual_risks: The role label is editorial taxonomy, but the third-party/CSLI refinement characterization is supported.
